<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fd2c76d6ce7ee8cd3267b3e026a1d48c400a73d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1039243c64b5236b485883dfe52c722270e49d57` — the merge of head `03c6a098a3993d02d9a8148520373430650de9d1` into base `5fd2c76d6ce7ee8cd3267b3e026a1d48c400a73d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

```sh

git fetch origin 1039243c64b5236b485883dfe52c722270e49d57 && git checkout 1039243c64b5236b485883dfe52c722270e49d57

the docs/spec search (`content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx:397-400, :945`, `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:355-381`, `docs/adr/0112-*`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json:264`); No file was written to `/home/user/objectstack`, no worktree or checkout was made, no test or build was run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The guard withholds exactly the ruled `details`, on both tools, and every other coded refusal is unchanged: right.** The one new line is `if (envelope.code === StandardErrorCode.enum.PERMISSION_DENIED) return errorResultWithCode(err);` (`mcp-http-tools.ts:336` at head); `errorResultWithCode` builds `{ code, message, status }` and never reads `details` (:363-366, :392-397). Both action catches call `errorResultFromThrown` and are byte-unchanged (`:1231-1233`, `:1325-1327`; the diff touches only :35-40 and :305-339). The class boundary matches the dispatcher's: `http-dispatcher.ts:2994` keys its withholding on `isPermissionDeniedError`, which is plugin-security's duck-typed matcher re-exported at `resolve-execution-context.ts:344` and defined at `plugin-security/src/errors.ts:337-345` (name `PermissionDeniedError` OR `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` OR the `[Security] Access denied` message prefix). The MCP guard keys on `code` alone, and in-tree that covers the same set: the class declares `code` as a constant (`errors.ts:42`), every duck-typed producer sets `name` and `code` together (`plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts:265-266`, `plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts:356-357`, `plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts:319-320`, `service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts:202-203`), and a message-prefix-only throw with no `code` makes `thrownRefusalEnvelope` answer `undefined` (:393-394), so its `details` are never read. `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` still serves the action and member: the new pin asserts it on both tools over the HTTP face (`mcp-action-refusal-details.test.ts:172-184`), and #15942's own pin (`mcp-action-confirmation-member.test.ts:149-161`) and `resume_run`'s (`mcp-resume-run-tool.test.ts:145-161`) are byte-unchanged. `resume_run`'s door-built `details` are also unchanged by reading: the only `PERMISSION_DENIED` that door builds carries `details: { code }` (`domains/automation.ts:2190`) or none (`domains/mcp.ts:988-993`), and `splitSemanticCode` turns a `{ code }`-only payload into `undefined` (`error-envelope.ts:108-113`), so `resumeDoorError` (`domains/mcp.ts:767-780`) never attached a `details` member to a `PERMISSION_DENIED`; the run artefacts ride the `FLOW_FAILED` row (`automation.ts:2192-2200`), a different code, still spread at :337-338.

2. **Keyed on a declared code through an existing export, not a denylist or a second policy copy; every in-tree producer of positions or permission sets in a refusal's `details` is a `PERMISSION_DENIED`: right.** The code is read from the spec's zod enum (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:53`, member at :79), exported through `packages/spec/src/api/index.ts:55` (`export * from './errors.zod'`) on the `@objectstack/spec/api` subpath that `packages/mcp/package.json` already depends on (`@objectstack/spec: workspace:*`). No key name of `details` is inspected; the class's answer is the existing `errorResultWithCode`, so the package holds one code-keyed question and no filter (:336-338). `packages/mcp` cannot import the dispatcher's own matcher (`@objectstack/mcp` depends on neither `@objectstack/runtime` nor `plugin-security`), so the spec code is the existing export available to it. Producers: every throw in `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` that puts `positions`/`permissionSets` into `details` is `new PermissionDeniedError(` (:2646-2652, :2775-2777, :2790-2793, :3039-3045, :3132-3139, :3210-3217, :3308-3311, :3318-3323, :3544-3546, :3694-3696, :3871-3875, :3930-3933, :3944-3947, :4227-4229). The other non-test files naming `permissionSets` (`rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`, `plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts`, `core/src/security/permission-manager.ts`, `core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`, `verify/src/parent-write-reach.ts`, `plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts`) put it in no thrown refusal's `details` (context grep returned nothing). One accuracy note on the dev's report, not on the code: it says the two duck-typed `PermissionDeniedError`s in service-storage and plugin-audit "carry no details" (true: `attachment-access-hooks.ts:201-206`, `comment-access-hooks.ts:318-323`), but two more duck-typed `PERMISSION_DENIED` producers do carry `details` (`{ object, fields, reason: 'field_predicate_denied' }` at `plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts:271` and `plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts:362`). They are query-side guards, not principal data, and the dispatcher and REST's closed list (`thrown-http-error.ts:234-241`) already withhold them, so the MCP guard withholding them is parity, not a defect.

3. **Option A (keep as built) is right for this PR; the residual fail-open is an Acceptance note, not a defect of this PR: right.** Option C needs an edit in `packages/runtime` (`domains/mcp.ts`'s `runAction` bridge), which the claim `6177192097` forbids ("No edit in `packages/runtime`, `packages/types` or `plugin-security`: reuse an existing export or stop"), so it is a new card, not this one. Option B (serve `details` only for `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`) would drop `resume_run`'s `FLOW_FAILED` run artefacts (`errorMessage`, `summary`, `runId`, `status`, `repairable`; `automation.ts:2195-2200`), which that file's own doc names as declared once in `@objectstack/spec/api` as `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` (:2173-2174) and which the console reads (:2154-2158); that narrows a declared contract the card never asked about. A closes exactly the ruled class with +24/-2 in one function. The residual (a future coded refusal carrying principal data would render its `details`) is shared with the dispatcher's own rule, which is also class-keyed (`isPermissionDeniedError`) and equally fail-open for a new class; REST's fail-closed shape lives in the runtime bridge (C), outside this claim. The PR records it in its acceptance notes and the report's out-of-scope finding (carrier none); whether to file C is the seat's call.

4. **The pin drives the real HTTP transport, asserts absence of the names in the whole serialized body, carries controls, and goes red on `origin/main`'s renderer: right.** It POSTs a JSON-RPC `tools/call` `Request` through `MCPServerRuntime.handleHttpRequest` with `{ bridge, parsedBody }` (`mcp-action-refusal-details.test.ts:124-140`), the same door and option the #15942 pin uses (`mcp-action-confirmation-member.test.ts:110-129`). The bridge double implements `listActions`, `runAction` and `resumeRun`, so `wireBridgeTools` registers both tools (`mcp-http-tools.ts:575-576`, `:1248-1249`), and the `resume_run` args `{ runId, values: {} }` fit the schema (:1283-1292). Assertions per denial row: strict `toEqual({ error: { code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', message, status: 403 } })` (:163-165), which fails on any extra member including `details` and the `developerMessage` sibling, and then `expect(raw).not.toContain(name)` for each of the four distinctive position and permission-set names against the raw HTTP response text (:166-169), so a renderer that moved the names to another key or into the message would still fail. Controls: the reader can `get_record` the row (:148-155) and `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`'s `details` stay served on both tools (:172-184). The sibling `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` rows for `run_action` and `resume_run` (`mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts:102-103, :165-172`) are the other non-permission coded control and are byte-unchanged. Red on main by reading: `origin/main`'s `errorResultFromThrown` (:312-317) spreads `details` verbatim, so both denial rows fail the strict shape and the `not.toContain` checks while the three controls pass, which is the dev's recorded run ("2 failed | 3 passed (5)") and the ablation's direction. `resume_run`'s row pins the shared renderer, not a measured producer, and the pin's header says so (:37-39).

5. **`@objectstack/mcp` `patch` with `Clause-②: no` is truthful; a permission refusal's `details` on a tool result is declared nowhere: right.** Searched `content/docs/**`, `docs/**` and `packages/spec/src/**`: the catalog's `PERMISSION_DENIED` entry is Cause/Fix/Retry only (`content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx:397-400`); the ledger is a list of codes with no `details` member for it (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`); the only MCP refusal with declared `details` is `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (#15942/#16293, ledger :355-365), which is untouched; the QA checklist already records that an MCP tool error carried no `details` on an FLS refusal and says to "never score on a details key" (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json:264`); the #7450 ruling makes REST's `{ message, code, object }` the contract for both transports (`permission-denied-envelope.ts:26-30`). The data tools' identical withholding landed as a `patch` in #23526 (`b1cfa3d263`). `code`, `message` and `status` are unchanged. Removing an undeclared member that a maintainer ruling keeps off the wire is a patch.

6. **PR body, changeset and the renderer's comment stay at function level; two lines in the pin name the route: right, with one flag.** The PR body names functions and files only (no route, request shape, payload or steps; its vitest excerpt shows the withheld response member's keys with the fixture names, which the card body itself already names). The changeset and the four commit messages carry no route token. The renderer's comment (`mcp-http-tools.ts:314-331`) is function-level. The pin's header line 28 ("The HTTP `/mcp` face") and the `describe` title at :147 ("over HTTP /mcp") name the route segment; the test code's the transport URL literal (withheld here by the seat, per the card's disclosure rule) and `tools/call` body (:125-133) are the same literals the sibling pins on main use (`mcp-action-confirmation-member.test.ts:111`) and are needed to drive the transport. Precedent on main already names `/mcp` in comments (`errorResultWithCode`'s doc at :356, `mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts:30`). Non-blocking: replace the two comment mentions with "the HTTP face" if the seat wants the file strictly route-free.

7. **Nothing else makes it unsafe to land: right.** Check-runs at the head, read last: 39 listed, 30 success, 6 skipped, 3 in progress (`Test Core` 1/6, 3/6, 4/6), none failed; `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` (and its four sub-checks), `Lint & Repo Gates` (and its eight sub-checks), `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size` and `Test Core` 2/6, 5/6, 6/6 are green. CJS/ESM: `@objectstack/spec`'s `./api` export has both `import` and `require` conditions (`packages/spec/package.json`), `packages/mcp/tsup.config.ts:12` builds `['esm', 'cjs']`, and `@objectstack/spec/api` is already imported from non-test source in `packages/runtime` (17 files), `packages/types` (4, also ESM+CJS), `packages/rest` (10) and eight other package groups, so the import has broad precedent. Typecheck: `StandardErrorCode.enum.PERMISSION_DENIED` is the literal `'PERMISSION_DENIED'` compared against a `string` (:336). The 62 related tests: the three sibling files are byte-unchanged (the PR's file list is exactly three paths). One stale comment outside the claim's surface: `mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts:79-81` still says the two action tools "render through `errorResultFromThrown`, which carries `details`", and its `actionDoor` exclusion (:83, :179) now skips a permission row that would pass for the action doors too; both sit outside the claimed file surface and are an acceptance note. The MCP renderer drops the withheld payload silently, whereas the dispatcher logs it server-side (`http-dispatcher.ts:3013-3017`); this matches the already-landed data-tools shape (`errorResultWithCode`, #23526) and is parity, not a regression.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/mcp`, as the changeset declares. The change removes an undeclared `details` member from two tool errors under a maintainer ruling that keeps it off the wire on every transport; `code`, `message` and `status` are unchanged, the declared `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` `details` are unchanged, and no exported signature, schema or documented contract moves. `Clause-②: no` is truthful. No other package is touched.

### ③ Verdict

PASS. No blocking item. Acceptance notes, none blocking: (a) the residual fail-open (a future coded refusal carrying principal data would still render its `details` on the two tools) is shared with the dispatcher's class-keyed rule and is recorded in the PR; the seat decides whether to file Option C (render `run_action`'s thrown errors through the runtime bridge's own builder, as `resumeDoorError` does) as a follow-up card, carrier none today; (b) `mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts:79-83` and its `actionDoor` exclusion at :179 are now partly stale and could lift the exclusion so one pin covers all twelve sites, outside this claim's surface; (c) the pin's header line 28 and `describe` title at :147 name `/mcp`; precedent on main does the same, so a reword to "the HTTP face" is optional; (d) two further duck-typed `PERMISSION_DENIED` producers carry non-principal `details` (`plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts:271`, `plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts:362`); the guard withholds them in parity with the dispatcher and REST, and the dev's report's "carry no details" sentence under-counts them without changing the result; (e) the MCP renderer drops the withheld payload with no server-side log line, matching the data tools since #23526; (f) three `Test Core` shards were still in progress when the check-runs were read, so the queue should see them complete green before merge.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6177192097` on #23529 · reviewed head `03c6a098a3993d02d9a8148520373430650de9d1` · 2026-10-14T21:13Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23544`: 223 changed lines). 3 files, +221 / −2. The `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review this seat took on the stricter reading is `6178628544`: PASS, nothing blocking. Clause-② is `no`.

1. **Shape.** Draft PR. The first line is `Fixes #23529`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at line start. The changeset is `@objectstack/mcp` `patch`, worded at function level.
2. **Scope against the dispatch** (triage `6177046363`).
   - The pin came first and failed on `main`: 2 failed, 3 passed. That is the runtime confirmation triage asked for.
   - The fix is one guard in `errorResultFromThrown`: a refusal whose declared code is the spec catalogue's `PERMISSION_DENIED` renders through `errorResultWithCode`, the data tools' one place. It is not a filter on key names, and there is no second policy copy in `packages/mcp`.
   - The `run_action` and `resume_run` catches are byte-unchanged.
   - No file outside the claim. The one added import line sits in the claimed file.
3. **Gates and evidence.**
   - **Pin and controls, after the fix:** 62/62 across the pin, `mcp-action-confirmation-member`, `mcp-coded-refusal` and `mcp-resume-run-tool`. The last three are byte-unchanged.
   - **Package suite:** `@objectstack/mcp` 467/467. Typecheck and build exit 0, and both the CJS and ESM dists load.
   - **Ablation:** deleting the guard turns only the two denial rows red, and the confirmation controls stay green. That shows the guard is keyed on the code and does not withhold blanket. The restore is proven.
   - **Local gates:** 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT MEASURED.
4. **The dev's open question (A / B / C): A, as built.**
   - It is the dispatch's second route.
   - B would drop `resume_run`'s declared `FLOW_FAILED` run artefacts (`ResumeFailureDetailsSchema`).
   - C needs a `packages/runtime` edit this claim forbids.
   - The class key matches the dispatcher's own. In-tree, every producer of a caller's positions or permission sets in `details` is a `PERMISSION_DENIED` (review ①2).
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.** These are Acceptance notes with `carrier:` none. Neither has measured reach, so neither passes the filing gate.
   - **The residual fail-open.** A future coded refusal carrying principal data would still render its `details` on the two tools. The dispatcher's class-keyed rule shares this, and C is its long-term home.
   - **A stale exclusion in another file.** `mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts:79-83` (and its `actionDoor` exclusion) is now partly stale.
   - The review's optional reword of two `/mcp` mentions in the pin's comments is not taken, because `main` has precedent for them.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) Every check is green or skipped by design: read at landing. One `Test Core` shard was in progress at this record.
   - (b) `mergeable_state` is clean at enqueue: read at landing.
